## What changed (read `git diff` for the exact text)

1. `scripts/movecheck/lines.mjs` — `isComment` is no longer a prefix test. It is a left-to-right scanner (`isCommentOnly`) that returns false when code appears outside every comment on the line. A leading `*` is taken as a continuation of a block comment opened earlier.
2. `scripts/movecheck/lines.mjs` — the ESM acceptance test is now a WHOLE-STATEMENT match (`IMPORT_STATEMENT` / `BARE_STATEMENT` / `REEXPORT_STATEMENT`, each `^…$`), not the end-anchor Lamoka verified in scratch. Nadine's reason: an end-anchored form still admits `} from './a'; evil(); import { b } from './c';`, which ENDS in a specifier. The clause between `import` and `from` is held to the character class `[\w$*,{}\s]` — no paren, quote, `=`, `.` or `;`. Two things are admitted after the specifier ON PURPOSE: an import-attribute clause (`with`/`assert { … }`, contents held to `[\w$'"\s:,.-]`) because this repo's server is Deno and a JSON import is ordinary there, and a trailing `//` comment.
3. `scripts/movecheck/lines.mjs` — `REQUIRE_BINDING`'s namelist is restricted for BOTH the object and the array form (`\{[\w$\s,:.]*\}|\[[\w$\s,.]*\]`), so no default expression can ride inside it.
4. `scripts/movecheck.mjs` — `--json` now emits `headers` and `isolated`; `--help` retracts the false claim that the header tail rule excludes a body, and says `--no-regions` costs the region shape too. **The `DELEGATION` tail rule was deliberately LEFT permissive — that is Spud's call, already settled, and is not yours to re-litigate.**
5. `test/movecheck.test.js` — seven new cases. `test/fixtures/movecheck/` — two waiver reasons corrected.

## Outcome
Accepted in full, and it earned its spawn on O1 alone. O1 is the third instance of this ticket's own defect shape and it was MINE: the comment allowance I added to TAIL to close a false alarm used a block-comment form that crosses newlines, so 'import { a } from "./x"; /*' swallowed 42 of 43 lines into the import class on both sides — and an old file whose 40-line header doc hung off one read clean, import:42, 0 unaccounted, which is the deleted-header-doc bug this tool exists to catch. I reproduced it before fixing it (the semicolon-first placement is load-bearing; my first attempt at the payload put the comment before the ';' and did not fire). Fixed the RULE rather than the placement: a comment inside a module statement may stand wherever whitespace may but may NOT span lines, which also closes the clause-side swallow f3ead9a had all along (25 of 25 lines, no payload ever written) — Osprey scoped its own fix to the tail because that half was the regression, and going wider costs nothing the repo-wide scan can see. Its second false alarm, a comment between the specifier and the ';', is real and is fixed by the same gap. Its first, 'const { PORT = 3000 }', I DECLINE as a finding and have documented in code as deliberate: 3000 is a value, and a value hiding in the import class is precisely what F3 was. O2 and O3 are correctly scored (both widenings are SyntaxErrors; the '*'-continuation assumption is safe for the reason Osprey gives rather than the one my comment gave, now written down), and its catch on the loadRoom waiver's closing parenthetical is right — 'collab' is const [collab] at room.ts:37, so the refactor I named cannot be written, which is the same wrong-mechanism failure the rewrite existed to remove, one round later. Cut and replaced with the two edits that CAN lose the phase. Its mutation check found the one invariant of mine pinned nowhere (a clause admitting parens), now pinned. Verified rather than asserted throughout, with the f3ead9a harness staged in scratch as its control, and it named the moving tree under it.
